Refinery Equipment Tender
A tender issued by oil refining companies for the procurement of complex process equipment used in petroleum refining operations.

Quick answer
A tender issued by oil refining companies for the procurement of complex process equipment used in petroleum refining operations.
Refinery equipment tenders are procurement exercises conducted by oil and gas companies, including public sector refiners like Indian Oil Corporation (IOC), Bharat Petroleum (BPCL), Hindustan Petroleum (HPCL), Chennai Petroleum (CPCL), and MRPL, for the purchase of capital equipment used in petroleum refining: distillation columns, heat exchangers, pressure vessels, pumps, compressors, reactors, and processing units.
What are Refinery Equipment Tenders in government procurement?
India operates 23 oil refineries with a combined processing capacity exceeding 250 million metric tonnes per annum. Both greenfield (new refinery) and brownfield (existing refinery expansion or upgrade) projects generate large equipment procurement volumes. IOC, BPCL, and HPCL together spend Rs 15,000-25,000 crore

al capability to meet ASME and API codes (often requiring third-party code approval by organisations like TÜV or Lloyds Register), competitive manufacturing cost (to match Chinese and European suppliers on price), and reliable quality track record (refineries remember past quality failures and delist vendors).
The Aatmanirbhar Bharat initiative and public sector PSU policies encourage Indian refinery companies to prefer domestically manufactured equipment. Companies like Bharat Heavy Electricals, L&T, Godrej, and several specialised vessel manufacturers have established themselves as preferred domestic suppliers, benefiting from this preference when specifications are otherwise met.
Example
IOCL Panipat Refinery floats a tender for supply of 28 heat exchanger shells and bundles for a new catalytic reformer unit under expansion. The specifications reference TEMA Type BEU and AEU, ASME Section VIII Div 1, with material as per ASME SA-240 316L stainless steel. Bidding is open to IOCL-approved vendors (a pre-qualification process). Three domestic vendors and two international vendors bid. The L1 domestic vendor, with IOCL QA approval, ASME U-stamp for unfired pressure vessels, and in-house shop inspection facility, wins. The equipment is manufactured, shop-tested, and inspected by IOCL's TPI (Third-Party Inspection) agency
